title: A verifier is a product: contract, version, verdicts with reasons, and abstention
design_ref: A verifier is a product: contract, interface and lifecycle
purpose: Read what each verifier service says about itself, send the strict math verifier five completions that exercise its contract, and try to start a training run on a verifier that has not been measured.

steps.display: for v in <the nine services>; do kubectl -n rewards exec deploy/$v -- GET 127.0.0.1:8080/info; done   # id, purpose, owner, code hash
steps.output:

Exactly one \boxed{} final answer after the reasoning; zero or several is FAIL. No 'or', 'either', 'maybe' or 'between' within 80 characters after the box. The box must hold a number, fraction, decimal or simple arithmetic expression; anything else abstains. Equality is symbolic (SymPy), so 1/2, 0.5, 2/4 and \frac{1}{2} are equal.

steps.display: kubectl -n rewards exec -i deploy/math-final-answer-2-0-0 -- POST /verify < five-completions.json

steps.output: REFUSED: math-final-answer@2.0.0 has no registry entry; measure it and run the gate first

checks.description: every service reports its own name@version, purpose, owner and a distinct code hash
checks.because: The code hash covers the verifier class, its version and its source files.

checks.description: one boxed answer passes; two boxes, a hedge and a missing box fail, each with its reason
checks.because: The contract allows exactly one box with no hedge word after it.

checks.description: an answer outside the accepted language abstains, with score 0, and every result names the verifier version
checks.because: Units inside the box are not in the narrow language; abstaining gives no reward instead of guessing. reward() turns it into None.

checks.description: a training run cannot pin a verifier that has no registry entry (exit 3)
checks.because: The launcher reads the registry before it writes the run's description or creates any Job.
